privacy.allowlist_rule: Resolve known resource routes to the family above, default deny for all others. Apply the same paths to request and response bodies, including arrays and JSON-in-string bodies. Unknown keys become the marker at any depth. Parent permission is not wildcard permission; arbitrary metadata, code, scripts, HTML, templates, URLs carrying bearers, provider options and all headers are never body-allowlisted. Query keys are separately allowlisted: page,per_page,include_totals,sort,fields,include_fields; all other query values are masked. Never log raw request URLs.
privacy.secret_read_rule: mgmt_api_read only for a successful GET whose authorized serializer returned credential material: clients client_secret; connections options credentials; actions secrets; emails credentials; keys private material (if ever supported); user identities access_token/refresh_token. Detection precedes scrubbing; no read event for the logs APIs or redacted-only results.
privacy.marker_evidence: Local marker: reviewed public sources do not establish one universal Auth0 marker; no live observation.
privacy.sink_secrets: Seal all fields marked secret; read substitutes marker. Omitted PATCH field preserves existing secret; literal marker on PATCH preserves a previously configured secret (local import/edit convention). New creates reject the marker as a secret. Endpoint URLs/headers are never included in delivery diagnostics.

stream_contract.start_from: ISO8601 RFC3339 datetime, create-only. Omitted=latest committed seq. Present=exclusive sequence before first retained event with Date >= supplied instant; persist internal StartFrom time.Time and skip Date<StartFrom in the worker while advancing checkpoint because Date and Seq may differ (local); if no match exists choose latest seq. stream_contract.failure_policy: 2xx acknowledges batch; all other responses and transport failures retry without bodies in diagnostics; 1s exponential to 300s; suspend after 24h continuously failing; resume retains checkpoint. Workers must skip filtered rows without stalling.

Public event table URL redirects to /docs/tenant-logs; 171 catalog entries plus 8 older filter-table entries and local legacy fapi form the frozen 180-row union. Future plans are owners for review, not commitments to implement Auth0-operated or retired features.

Current catalog categorizes fco as other although older filters say auth.login.fail; catalog wins. fapi has no current code row: retained solely for explicit spec middleware requirement; management.fail is a documented category.
Global logs public scope list includes read:logs and read:logs_users without resolving alternative/conjunctive meaning; local spec uses read:logs globally and both for a user route.
Public page body calls the Lucene parameter q but embedded OpenAPI labels it search; local wire parameter remains q for pinned SDK/CLI compatibility. search is not an accepted alias.

Checkpoint from overrides q and ignores projection/totals/sort/page as explicitly documented. take-only recent mode is local, ascending sequence. Two-second settlement is local and cannot by itself prove commit-order safety; stores must serialize assignment and commit visibility.
No universal upstream redaction marker, per-resource body allowlist, sink-secret read marker or PATCH marker semantics proven; all frozen as conservative local behavior.

Daily default 7 days inclusive and max 366 days, empty-day rows and totals count capped at 1000 are local bounds; upstream max/default not stated in reviewed docs. Stats codes count s/ssa/sepft once per successful login, ss once per registration, each breach code once. Token exchanges do not double-count logins.

startFrom is an ISO8601 datetime in public API, not a log ID. Persist internal StartFrom time.Time in storage/SQL/protobuf; worker skips older Date rows while advancing checkpoint. Public reads omit startFrom. This extends the shared storage model for exact replay under Date/Seq skew.
Public vendor APIs establish accepted requests, not Auth0 private adapter mappings. Exact envelope/tag mappings above are local and need mock verification; no vendor accounts were called.

Log ID 56 decimal digits and sequence encoding, query subset bounds, cloud suspension, and runtime policies are local compatibility choices, not claims about Auth0 internals.
